en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 13.22.
Sanidassanattika (The Triplet on the Visible)
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and impinging, a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor impinging arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and impinging, a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor impinging arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and impinging, a state that is neither demonstrable nor impinging arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and impinging, states that are both not non-demonstrable-and-impinging and neither demonstrable-nor-impinging arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and impinging, a state that is neither demonstrable-nor-impinging... [arises].
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, states that are neither demonstrable nor reactive arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and reactive, states that are neither demonstrable and reactive nor non-demonstrable and non-reactive arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, a state that is neither demonstrable nor reactive arises by way of the root condition... [six].

Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-demonstrable and impinging (*anidassana-sappaṭigha*) and a phenomenon that is non-demonstrable and non-impinging (*anidassana-appaṭigha*), a phenomenon that is non-demonstrable and impinging arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). ... [Six combinations. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are eighteen;

under object-condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are three ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition (*avigata*) there are eighteen. (The full detail applies everywhere. The section on co-nascence (*sahajāta-vāra*) ... pe ... and the section on association (*sampayutta-vāra*) should also be expanded. Root-object.
A non-demonstrable and non-reactive state is a condition for a non-demonstrable and non-reactive state by way of the root-cause condition.
A non-demonstrable and non-reactive state is a condition for a non-demonstrable but reactive state by way of the root-cause condition.
A non-demonstrable and non-reactive state is a condition for a non-demonstrable but reactive state by way of the root-cause condition.

A non-demonstrable and non-reactive state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither demonstrable nor reactive and for a state that is neither demonstrable nor non-reactive.

A non-demonstrable and non-reactive state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither demonstrable nor reactive and for a state that is neither demonstrable nor non-reactive. A non-demonstrable and non-reactive...
A state that is both visible and impinging is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is not visible and impinging, and for a state that is neither visible nor impinging.
A state that is both visible and impinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not visible and impinging... [three] (abbreviated). Under root-condition there are six;
under object-condition, nine; under predominance-condition, twelve; under proximity-condition, three... [etc. ... under conascence-condition, eighteen.

With respect to mutuality, there are thirteen; with respect to dependence, eighteen; with respect to strong-dependence, nine; with respect to prenascence, eighteen; with respect to postnascence, six; with respect to repetition, three;
with respect to kamma, resultant, and nutriment, six; with respect to faculty, nine; with respect to jhāna and path, six; with respect to association, three;
with respect to dissociation, nine …pe… with respect to non-disappearance, twenty-seven. (The Chapter of Questions should be expanded.)
